answer: Reputation graphs rank agents by earned trust rather than headcount, so a fresh identity starts at the nadir of credibility and must win real endorsements to rise. A sybil attacker needs a plume of genuine high-reputation backers for each clone, each one costly to cultivate and impossible to fake. The dawn of trust is slow to build but instant to lose on bad behavior. Per-identity cost thus makes mass spawning economically suicidal for any bot farm.
